title: Tenant Admin Onboarding Triage Rubric & Escalation Flow for Enterprise Identity Requests
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers report inconsistent turnaround and incorrect routing for admin & access requests (RBAC role grants, SSO config requests, SCIM provisioning onboarding, org-level policy exceptions). Objective: Define a deterministic triage rubric and escalation flow that non-engineering support staff can use to classify requests, automatically route to the correct owner (support, solutions, infra, sales engineering), and provide SLAs per class. Scope: triage rubric, routing table, required intake fields, initial UI copy for Console request form, canary rollout plan. Out of scope: backend implementation of SCIM connectors and RBAC enforcement logic (ENG teams to implement later).
acceptance_criteria: A single-page triage rubric that maps incoming request attributes to one of five handling buckets (self-serve, support, solutions, SRE/infra, security)
Routing table with routing rules expressed as matchers (e.g., org size >10k AND SCIM=true -> solutions) and recommended SLA per bucket
Console request form wireframes with required fields validated against rubric (mock in Figma) and API contract for intake service
Runbook for support and on-call rotation with clear handoffs and escalation path to engineering within target SLA
Pilot with two enterprise accounts and measurement plan (latency to first response, resolution time, misroute rate)

notes: Design trade-off: keep intake form short to reduce friction; prefer follow-up clarifying questions via support ticket over many required fields.
Routing heuristics should be editable by Support leads through Console in future (not in initial rollout).
Consideration: classify incidental SSO certificate updates as low-risk self-serve with guardrails; certificate rotation requests flagged for security review.
